inputs.text: The Liberal Party is showing fractures from within as some MPs push for a leadership rethink, but the real issue is how certain figures are trying to drag the party toward higher taxes on gas companies and ending concessions that benefit property investors. Angus Taylor has flatly rejected Andrew Hastie’s call for the party to be “open-minded” about these changes, which is the correct stand if we want to preserve economic strength built on personal responsibility rather than chasing progressive notions of fairness that punish success and erode family wealth. The opposition leader was right to refuse backing Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump, showing resistance to the usual left-wing attacks on a leader who prioritizes national interests. At the same time, the failure to clearly support the US and Israel’s war with Iran undercuts the authority needed to confront real threats and maintain order.
